deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.101): Hilbert plans to carry Riemann's theory over to n dimensions. Riemann's theory is that of the many-sheeted 2-dimensional surfaces belonging to an algebraic function of one variable. On p.101 he states that a continuous function can be single-valued exactly when the domain is simply connected. He even proposes to define simple connectivity this way: every continuous function on the domain is single-valued.

Setup:
- Take n-dimensional space R^n (or S^n).
- Prescribe a branching locus B, on which the functions are left undefined. B is necessarily of dimension n-2.
- Introduce cuts S_i of dimension n-1 (they must separate space), bounded only by B.

This page continues the setup:
(1) The cuts may meet one another, or abut, along certain (n-2)-dimensional sets.
(2) They are to be placed so that X' = R^n \ (B ∪ ⋃S_i) is simply connected.
(3) On the simply connected X' one can construct single-valued continuous functions u, v, w 'of the kind described at the beginning'. This refers to an earlier part of the notebook, presumably coordinate-like or harmonic functions.
(4) B may be reducible: B = B_1 ∪ … ∪ B_k with B_j irreducible.
(5) To each B_j a positive integer ν_j, 'the period', is attached. The function is reproduced after ν_j circuits, and not earlier, around an infinitely small circle linking B_j (a meridian).
   - In modern terms, the local monodromy around B_j has order exactly ν_j, i.e. ν_j is the ramification index.
   - The simplest case is all ν_j = 2.
(6) The first problem: how many-valued is a function with the given branching locus and periods?
   - Equivalently: how many copies of space must be stacked so that, after suitable gluing along the cuts (finished on p.103), a single-valued, everywhere continuous function exists on the resulting 'Riemann space'?

Modern formulation (mine):
- Find the possible degrees d, in particular the minimal one, of connected branched coverings M → S^n branched along B with ramification index ν_j over B_j.
- Equivalently, find transitive homomorphisms ρ: π1(S^n \ B) → S_d in which every meridian of B_j maps to a permutation of order ν_j. A meridian is a small loop around B_j joined to a basepoint; the order condition means all cycles have length ν_j if the covering is to be 'regular' over B_j.
- The cuts S_i realize the covering combinatorially. The sheets are d copies of X', and the gluing across each cut is given by the monodromy permutation.

On p.103 Hilbert specializes:
- n = 3, B a knotted closed curve, ν = 2.
- The first cut is a surface spanning the knot, in effect a Seifert-type surface.
- Further 'plugging' cuts follow, illustrated by a physical model he built.
- This is the double branched cover of S^3 along a knot.

Implicit fact (mine): no derivation or computation appears on this page; it is a program statement.
errors: No computational errors; the page is programmatic.

Unstated subtlety 1: an (n-1)-dimensional cut bounded only by B does not in general make the complement simply connected. For a nontrivial knot, the complement of a Seifert surface has non-free (nontrivial) fundamental group. Additional cuts are needed, and Hilbert indeed adds 'verstopfen' cuts on the next page.

Unstated subtlety 2: the question 'how many-valued' has no unique answer from B and the ν_j alone. Many coverings with different degrees exist. Only the minimal degree, or the classification of all coverings via representations of π1(complement), is well-posed.

Unstated subtlety 3: H1(S^n \ B) is generated by the meridians. A cyclic covering whose degree is the lcm of the ν_j always exists only under suitable homological conditions (e.g., one component, or compatible ν_j). Hilbert does not address existence.
'Reproduces after ν circuits' presumes every cycle of the local monodromy has length ν. In general, sheets over B_j can have different ramification, so this is an extra (regularity) assumption.

results.what: Generalization of Riemann surfaces to n-dimensional branched coverings of R^n/S^n, branched along a codimension-2 locus with prescribed ramification indices, constructed by cutting along codimension-1 cuts to a simply connected domain and gluing sheets
results.modern_name: Branched coverings of manifolds / higher-dimensional Riemann existence problem (monodromy representations of π1 of the complement of a codim-2 set)
results.usually_credited_to: Heegaard (dissertation 1898, double branched covers of S^3 over knots), Wirtinger (1905, branched covers along knots in connection with algebraic functions of two variables), Tietze (1908), Alexander (1920)

results.what: Characterization/definition of simple connectivity as: every continuous function (local branch) is single-valued (from preceding page, used here)
results.modern_name: Monodromy theorem / simply connected iff all coverings trivial
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Weierstrass (monodromy theorem); Poincaré 1895 for fundamental group in higher dimensions

results.what: Problem of determining the minimal sheet number of a covering with given branch locus and periods (simplest case all ν=2)
results.modern_name: Existence/degree of branched covers with prescribed branching data (Hurwitz problem in higher dimensions); double branched covers
results.usually_credited_to: Hurwitz (1891) in dimension 2; Heegaard/Wirtinger for knots in dimension 3

deep.surprise_reason: If this notebook dates from c.1890 (bundle 600 notebooks span the late 1880s–1890s), Hilbert is here formulating the theory of branched coverings of 3-space along knotted curves, with spanning surfaces and a physical model. That would be before Heegaard (1898) and Wirtinger (1905), who are usually credited with initiating this. Hilbert's interest in topology and knots is known to some historians (e.g. via Dehn and the Göttingen milieu), so it is not unheard of. The page itself is only a program statement, without results. Hence a notable but not major finding.

checkable.asserts: Determinant of the trefoil (Alexander polynomial at -1) is 3, so the double branched cover (all ν=2, Hilbert's simplest case for a knotted curve) has H1 = Z/3; the double cover exists and is the lens space L(3,1).
Figure-eight knot: double branched cover has |H1| = 5 (lens space L(5,2)); illustrates that a degree-2 cover always exists for a knot, since H1(complement)=Z maps onto Z/2.
Riemann–Hurwitz sanity check for the n=2 case Hilbert generalizes: a 2-sheeted cover of the sphere with 4 branch points of period 2 has genus 1.
